source.question: Why did well F-12 decline faster after 2010? Compare with the 2005 development plan.

note: Oct 28 night (seventh panel): verdict changed on purpose by the new rules (a conclusion drawn with ', so' in a fact). Oct 29 (seventh panel): verdict changed on purpose (a conclusion drawn with ', so' in a fact; a gradual shift's period-mean change written as a fall at a date). Oct 30 (tenth panel): verdict changed on purpose: a period's mean written as the level on one day.

submission.summary: F-12’s oil rate most likely collapsed after mid-2010 because injection water broke through and then took most of its liquid capacity, not because of a sudden operational step; its decline after breakthrough was about 0.45 per year while it produced flat before.

findings.claim: F-12’s oil rate fell 72% around 2010-07-18, from 4 050 to 1 146 Sm3/d (weekly mean).
findings.detail: Regime change oil_rate around 2010-07-18: before_mean 4050 -> after_mean 1146, relative_change -0.7171; across 4 weeks each side 2352 -> 1838 (-21.85%), so gradual not a step. Source detect_events.

findings.claim: Water cut rose from 3% to 51% around 2010-02-14 and then to 81% around 2010-10-24.
findings.detail: water_cut regime 0.02896 -> 0.5134 (+0.4845) around 2010-02-14; then 0.5134 -> 0.8141 (+0.3006) around 2010-10-24. Thresholds: 5% on 2009-10-31 (20.6 months after first oil), 50% on 2010-06-04, 80% on 2012-02-14 (48.06 months after first oil).

findings.claim: Before breakthrough F-12 produced flat at 0.0545 per year, after it declined at about 0.45 per year.
findings.detail: Fit 2008-02-13 to 2010-07-17 exponential qi 4166 Sm3/d, di 0.0545/yr, r2_log 0.01813 poor fit (plateau) - warnings; fit 2010-07-18 to 2012-12-08 exponential qi 1798, di 0.446/yr, r2_log 0.8726, rmse_log 0.1185, hyperbolic b 0.06386 close to exponential.

findings.claim: Liquid stayed high while water took capacity and the choke opened to 100%, with reservoir pressure supported.
findings.detail: By year liquid rate 3502 (2008) -> 4740 (2009) -> 5130 (2010) -> 5260 (2012) Sm3/d; choke 41.85% -> 59.88% -> 53.17% -> 100.0% in 2012; water cut 0.57 in 2010 to 0.86 in 2012. Field voidage replacement_ratio 1.08 in 2010, 1.02 in 2011-2012 (reservoir conditions Bo 1.385), so injection kept pace.

findings.claim: Production logs showed oil from the upper perforations and water from below, so the 2010 plug at 3210 m could only remove about 1% of oil and 33% of water.
findings.detail: PLT 2009-03: ~83% of oil from upper 2 completions, oil inflow 3135-3221 m. PLT 2010-09: oil comes_in 3132-3165 m, water comes_in 3165-3243 m. At 3210 m below share: low rate oil 0.011 water 0.325, medium oil 0.015 water 0.376; at 3150 m oil 0.808/0.734 water 0.971/1.0. Plug 5.72" EVO installed 2010-09-23 at 3210 m mid element.

findings.claim: The 2005 plan expected water breakthrough after about 2 years at about 6 MSm3; F-12 broke through after 21 months.
findings.detail: PUD p.23 exact quotes: 'Vannproduksjonen kommer først og fremst fra injeksjonsvannet som bryter gjennom i brønnene etter omlag 2 år.' [Water production comes primarily from injection water that breaks through in the wells after about 2 years.] and 'På det tidspunkt er kumulativ oljeproduksjon omlag 6 MSm3' [At that time cumulative oil production is about 6 MSm3]. F-12 5% threshold 2009-10-31 cum 2401970 Sm3 (~2.4 million), 50% 2010-06-04 (27.69 months), 80% 2012-02-14. Platform design maximum water cut 0.80 (Maksimum vannkutt 0,80, Maks vanninnhold 80%). Field reached 0.80 in 2012-06, never exceeded liquid 13000 or water handling 10400 Sm3/d.

issues.text: water cut above 0.80 (now 0.85); the platform was designed for 0.80
oil rate 60% lower in the period after than before (weekly mean 1,259 -> 509 Sm3/d), a gradual change: 23% across it
31 days shut in over the last 180

result.no_trend: WOR is not rising with cumulative oil on 2013-05 to 2016-08: no limit can be projected
result.notes: WOR = water/oil by month; the trend is log10(WOR) against cumulative oil, fitted on up to 36 recent months with WOR >= 1. field_voidage: replacement_ratio is injection over voidage at reservoir conditions (Bo 1.385 m3/Sm3 from PUD p.20, low/high with Bo 1.5/1.27; Bw 1; above the bubble point, so no free gas); surface_ratio is the same in surface volumes, which overstates replacement.

volve_pud.title: Plan for utbygging og drift av Volve (PUD, plan for development and operation)

rows: The table row shows water treatment 10,400 m3/d and gas lift 0.45 MSm3/d as design capacities.
The table row shows total liquid treatment 13,000 m3/d and water injection 16,000 m3/d as design capacities.
Total væske behandling | 13.000 m3/d | Vanninjeksjon | 16.000 m3/d
The Volve oil field is located in block 15/9 ca. 200 km west of Stavanger and ca. 8 km north of the Sleipner A platform with water depth in the area of ca. 90 m.
Volve er et oljefelt beliggende i blokk 15/9 ca 200 km vest for Stavanger og ca 8 km nord av Sleipner A plattformen, se figur 1.1. Vanndypet i området er ca. 90 m.

The process plant on the jack-up platform is designed for the following capacities: oil production 9,000 Sm3/d, rich gas 1.5 MSm3/d, water treatment 10,400 m3/d, gas lift 0.45 MSm3/d, total liquid treatment 13,000 m3/d and water injection 16,000 m3/d.
Prosessanlegget på den oppjekkbare plattformen er designet for følgende kapasiteter.
The gas is transferred in a 7.4" pipeline via subsea template D on the Sleipner Øst field and further to the SLA facilities.
Gassen overføres i en 7.4" rørledning via havbunnsramme D på Sleipner Øst feltet og videre inn til SLA anleggene.
The field water injection capacity is 16000 Sm3/d.
The field maximum water cut is 0,80.
The well oil rate limit is 2500-4500 Sm3/d.

result.unit: million Sm3 (MSm3) of oil per calendar year, whole field
result.plan_source: Plan for utbygging og drift av Volve (PUD, plan for development and operation), page 25, Table 4.5
result.note: years: calendar years. The plan assumed first oil in March 2007 and the field started in February 2008, so by_production_year compares each year of production with the plan's year of the same number (plan 2007 with field 2008).

result.scope: whole field, all producers and injectors summed per day, then per month
result.plan_source: Plan for utbygging og drift av Volve (PUD, plan for development and operation), page 23, Table 4.3

water_sm3_per_day.limit: field water handling (derived: liquid capacity x maximum water cut)

result.plan_end_quote: Kumulativ oljeproduksjon inntil minimum økonomisk rate på 2.100 Sm3 /d (gitt Volve oljepris på 18,7 USD/fat) nås er 11,4 MSm3
result.note: These are field and platform limits (PUD p.35 lists the same platform capacities); compare them with field totals, never one well. The maximum water cut is a share at full liquid rate: the water the platform can handle is liquid capacity x maximum water cut (water_sm3_per_day). The field reaching that share at a lower liquid rate means it ran at the design water cut, not over its water capacity. Rates are per calendar day of each month.

surveys.read_from: LAS files of the interpreted log (Well_logs_pr_WELL/15_9-F-12/10.PRODUCTION LOGS/PLT Sept 2010)

result.note: A production log measures the flow passing each depth while the well flows; going up, it grows past each zone that produces. A share at a depth is the part of the pass's oil or water entering below that depth (1 at the bottom of the well's inflow, 0 above the top zone). comes_in_from_m to to_m holds 90% of each phase's inflow. Only shares are given: the files' rates have no units, and the plots' are downhole volumes. A plug set at a depth shuts off what enters below it: the shares below say what it could remove. Each survey's passes were run at several surface rates. A survey read off pictures carries the checks of that reading.
